content: The French inhale is a smoking trick that involves taking a deep drag of smoke, then allowing the smoke to drift out of the mouth while it remains open. As the smoke wafts out, the individual inhales through their nose, effectively drawing the smoke back into their respiratory system from the air. This creates a visual effect where the smoke appears to flow upward from the mouth to the nose. Some people refer to this technique as an Irish Waterfall due to the visual illusion of the smoke moving in an upward direction, which humorously contrasts with the traditional concept of a waterfall. The term Irish Waterfall also plays on old jokes suggesting that anything Irish is backwards. This particular trick is often performed in combination with another popular smoking trick, the smoke ring, to enhance the visual appeal and complexity of the performance.
